04 / INTERVALS

A note becomes
a chord.

Choose the flavour. The root tells you where home is; the third gives the mood; the fifth gives the chord its frame.

ROOT / 1

Home

The note the chord is named after. Everything is heard in relation to it.

THIRD / 3 or ♭3

Mood

Major thirds feel open; minor thirds pull inward. One fret changes the colour.

FIFTH / 5 or ♭5

Frame

The perfect fifth sounds stable. Flatten it and the chord becomes diminished.

WHY IT SOUNDS THAT WAY

The distance is
the character.

Intervals are measured in semitones — one fret at a time. The same two notes can feel settled or tense depending on their distance and musical context.

STABILITYCONSONANT
More colour and roughness →

“Dissonant” doesn’t mean wrong. It means the sound creates motion or asks for resolution. Style, voicing, volume and what comes next all change how tense an interval feels.

07 / MODES

One scale.
Seven centres.

Modes are not seven unrelated patterns. They are seven ways of making a different note feel like home — each with one interval that reveals its colour.

CHARACTERISTIC TONEMajor seventh

RootCharacteristicRoute tones
One playable octave · tap any tone

The useful shortcut: compare every mode with a major or natural-minor scale from the same root. Dorian is minor with a natural 6; Lydian is major with a sharp 4; Mixolydian is major with a flat 7.
